subject: rove beetle
title: This 5-Millimeter Beetle Rockets Across Water Without Using Its Legs

scenes.text: This beetle crosses water without moving a single leg.
This rove beetle is under five millimeters long and hunts at the water's edge.
If it lands on water and something attacks, it shoots away at about seventy centimeters a second.
Scaled up to your size, that's hundreds of miles an hour.
The trick is at its rear end. A chemical weakens the water's skin behind it.
The water ahead pulls harder, and the beetle is dragged forward. No legs needed.

description:
Stenus rove beetles, under 5 mm long, can escape across water at up to about 70 cm per second without using their legs, roughly 370 to 560 mph if scaled to human size.
They release a secretion from the tip of the abdomen that lowers the surface tension behind them, so the stronger surface tension ahead pulls them forward.
Which tiny animal has the strangest way of moving?
first_comment: It can only do this a few times before its chemical runs out. Which animal would you want this trick for?
